title: Adani Airports Raises $1 Billion From Temasek, BlackRock and Premji Invest at $18 Billion Valuation
excerpt: India's largest airport operator sold a 5.54% stake to a global investor consortium, valuing the business at nearly twice rival GMR Airports and more than Heathrow.
body:
• Adani Airport Holdings raised approximately $1 billion (₹9,825 crore) by selling a 5.54% stake to Temasek, BlackRock, Premji Invest and Alpha Wave Global
  • The deal values the airport operator at $18 billion pre-money — nearly twice rival GMR Airports and more than Heathrow or Paris-Charles de Gaulle
  • Funds will be deployed for airport modernisation, 22 million sq ft of mixed-use airport city development and expansion to 200 million annual passengers
  • The fundraise follows Adani Enterprises' ₹15,000 crore qualified institutional placement in July, India's largest by a non-financial corporate

Adani Airport Holdings Limited, India's largest private airport operator, has raised approximately $1 billion from a consortium of four global investors in what represents the first external equity investment in the business.

Adani Enterprises, the group's flagship company and AAHL's parent, announced on Wednesday that it had agreed to sell up to a 5.54 percent stake in the airport unit to a group comprising Singapore's Temasek, BlackRock, Premji Invest and Alpha Wave Global. The deal values AAHL at $18 billion before the investment, or roughly $19 billion after the capital infusion.

Marquee Investor Consortium

The investor group comprises Temasek's Jongsong Investments, Alpha Wave III, Premji Invest's PI Opportunities funds, and funds managed by BlackRock across global allocation, strategic income and fixed-income strategies. The capital will be invested in three tranches, with the final tranche expected to close by July 2027.

Several of the investors bring existing aviation exposure. Premji Invest is a backer of SNV Aviation-owned Akasa Air, having participated in the airline's $125 million fundraise in 2025. Temasek is the majority shareholder in Singapore Airlines, which holds a 25.1 percent stake in Air India.

"India's aviation sector is one of the most powerful multipliers of the country's GDP growth. Every expansion in air connectivity catalyses trade, tourism, employment and regional development well beyond the airport gate."

— Jeet Adani, Non-Executive Director, AAHL

Valuation Sets New Benchmark

At $19 billion post-money, AAHL is now more valuable than marquee global operators including Paris-based Aéroports de Paris ($12.5 billion) and London's Heathrow Airport Holdings ($11.8 billion). Its valuation is nearly double that of listed rival GMR Airports, which had a market capitalisation of approximately $10.8 billion on Wednesday.

Adani Enterprises' own market capitalisation stood at $43.5 billion, meaning the airports business now accounts for roughly 43 percent of the flagship company's value. AAHL is widely expected to be the next Adani entity to pursue a public-market listing.

Where the Money Goes

AAHL manages eight airports — Mumbai, Navi Mumbai, Ahmedabad, Jaipur, Lucknow, Guwahati, Mangaluru and Thiruvananthapuram — handling approximately 25 percent of India's passenger traffic and 33 percent of its air cargo volumes.

The ₹9,825 crore infusion will fund three strategic priorities: modernising and expanding existing airport infrastructure to serve 200 million passengers annually, developing roughly 22 million square feet of mixed-use real estate in the first phase of the Adani Airport City programme, and scaling ground handling and other non-aeronautical businesses.

The airport city developments will span Mumbai, Navi Mumbai, Ahmedabad, Lucknow, Jaipur and Guwahati, including hotels, retail centres, office space and entertainment venues integrated with airport infrastructure.

Financial Performance Strengthening

The fundraise comes on the back of improving financials. AAHL reported revenue of ₹13,081 crore in FY26, up 28 percent from ₹10,224 crore the previous year. EBITDA surged 55 percent to ₹5,394 crore, while profit before tax reached ₹1,427 crore. Passenger traffic rose modestly to 95.3 million from 94.4 million.

Non-aeronautical revenue grew 31 percent in FY26, outpacing the 26 percent growth in aeronautical revenue, reflecting the company's push to diversify income streams.

Bigger Ambitions Ahead

The deal follows Adani Enterprises' ₹15,000 crore qualified institutional placement in July, India's largest QIP by a non-financial corporate. The airport business has also previously tapped global debt markets, raising $750 million through external commercial borrowings in June 2025.

India is preparing to award 11 government-owned airports under 50-year public-private partnership concessions, potentially attracting about ₹8,622 crore of private investment. AAHL has publicly stated its intention to bid for all 11.

Adani Enterprises shares gained 5.1 percent on Wednesday following the announcement, even as the broader market fell sharply.
